latest.title: New Convertible Loan Note Facility
latest.content:
Today 16:18
RNS Number : 0403L
Critical Metals PLC
03 July 2026
Critical Metals plc / EPIC: CRTM / Market: Main Market
3 July 2026
Critical Metals plc
("Critical Metals" or the "Company")
New Convertible Loan Note Facility
Critical Metals plc (LSE:CRTM), a mining company established to acquire mining opportunities in the critical and strategic metals sector, which operates the Molulu Copper/Cobalt Project ("Molulu") in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announces that it has agreed with NIU Invest SE ("NIU"), the Company's majority shareholder, that it will subscribe for £2,500,000 convertible loan notes under a new convertible loan note instrument ("CLN Instrument") on similar terms to the £2,100,000 convertible loan instrument that the Company created in December 2025 ("2025 CLN Instrument"). The Company has not issued all of notes under this instrument and the remaining notes will be subscribed for by NIU at par by the end of September 2026. The funds raised under the CLN Instrument and the 2025 CLN Instrument is intended to provide the Company with the capital it needs for at least the next 12 months and will be used to explore acquisition opportunities in the mining sector, fund exploration and/or production activities at Molulu and for general working capital.
On 3 July 2026 NIU agreed to subscribed for £2,500,000 of convertible loan notes issued under the 2025 CLN Instrument at par at the following times:
(i)
£1,100,000 on or before 31 December 2026;
(ii)
£1,000,000 on or before 31 May 2027; and
(iii)
£400,000 to applied to repay the sums due under the facility provided to the Company by NIU in July 2025.
The main terms of the 2025 CLN Instrument is as follows:
·
Mature on 18 month from issue of the relevant notes;
·
Interest at 10% per annum, payable on maturity;
·
Are convertible into ordinary shares of the company at a conversation price of 10.25 per Ordinary Share of £0.0005 each in the capital of the Company ("Ordinary Shares"), which is the same conversion price as under the CLN instrument; and
·
May be redeemed at the noteholder's option at any time subject to certain restrictions and will be repayable in cash at the end of the term.
·
There are certain customary events resulting in immediate redemption related to solvency type issues.
The issue of the notes under the 2025 CLN Instrument to NIU is a material related party transaction for the purposes of DTR 7.3.6 due to NIU's shareholding in the Company representing in excess of 60.00% of the issued Ordinary Shares.
Danilo Lange, CEO of Critical Metals, said:
"We are pleased to have secured a further commitment from NIU to provide capital to help us develop the Company's business."
**ENDS**
For further information on the Company please visit

or contact:

About Critical Metals
London listed Critical Metals plc is focused on identifying low CAPEX and OPEX brown-field projects with near-term production and cash-flow, concentrating on minerals that have strategic importance to future global economic growth. In line with this, and with an off-take partner already in place, the Company is currently focused on recommencing production at the formerly producing Molulu Copper/Cobalt Project in the Katangan Copperbelt in Democratic Republic of Congo ('DRC').

latest.content:

Critical Metals plc / EPIC: CRTM / Market: Main Market
12 May 2026
Critical Metals Plc
("Critical Metals" or the "Company")
Board Changes
Critical Metals plc (
LSE:CRTM)
, a mining company established to acquire mining opportunities in the critical and strategic metals sector, currently developing the Molulu Copper/Cobalt Project ("Molulu") in the Democratic Republic of Congo, announces the permanent appointment of Mr Danilo Lange as Chief Executive Officer, with immediate effect.
Mr Lange, an experienced international executive with over 25 years of leadership experience across mining, consumer goods, and marketing sectors, had served as the Company's Interim CEO since December 2025.
Kelvin Williams, Non-Executive Chairman, said:
"
We are very pleased that Danilo has agreed to continue as Chief Executive Officer on a permanent basis following his appointment as interim CEO in December 2025. During this period, he has demonstrated a clear understanding of the business. His experience and performance in the role made him the best candidate for the role."
Mr Danilo Lange, CEO of Critical Metals plc, added:
"I am delighted to be appointed as the CEO of Critical Metals on a permanent basis. I would like to take the opportunity to thank the board for their support and look forward to advancing on our stated strategy, to invest in low-capex, close to production projects with exposure to critical metals."
**ENDS**

company_30s.what_they_do: Critical Metals Plc is a mining company that focuses on extracting copper and other critical metals from a mine in the UK. The operation is still in early stages – the company has only shipped a small amount of ore from the site and is working on turning the mine into a commercial producer.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Copper and other critical metals are the backbone of the green‑tech supply chain. Governments and industry are pushing for new sources of these metals, so any company that can supply them has a strategic niche. If Critical Metals can prove the mine is viable, it could become an important supplier for battery makers, wind turbines and other renewable‑energy infrastructure.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a precarious phase. It has had a recent suspension of trading, has issued convertible loan notes, and is undergoing board and shareholder changes. Operations appear stalled, but a large shareholder has been buying shares, which may indicate an upcoming catalyst. The stock is currently trading near the bottom of its recent range.

rns_narrative: The company has been shuffling its board and raising capital through a convertible loan facility. A significant shareholder change suggests that the firm is trying to shore up its balance sheet. Meanwhile, a regulatory suspension has halted trading, adding uncertainty about the mine’s operational status.

These events cluster around two themes: (1) a financial restructuring that could unlock cash, and (2) a regulatory hurdle that must be cleared before the mine can resume production. Both are necessary steps for the company to move from a stalled project to a revenue‑generating operation.
If the regulatory clearance comes through and the new capital is deployed, the company could start production, which would be a clear catalyst for a price bounce.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bullish chatter focuses on the second‑largest shareholder’s buying spree and the possibility that the stock is being held by smart money for a squeeze. Some traders believe the company’s low price is a buying opportunity once the mine’s status is clarified.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the suspension, the lack of proven ore, and the company’s heavy reliance on debt‑financed notes. They worry that the mine may never become commercially viable and that the stock could be delisted.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Initially quiet, sentiment has shifted toward cautious optimism as the large shareholder’s purchases become visible, but the overall mood remains uncertain because of the regulatory hold‑up.

near_term_catalysts: Regulatory clearance that lifts the trading suspension and allows the mine to resume operations.
An announcement of a new resource estimate that confirms the mine’s commercial viability.
Conversion of the convertible notes into equity, which would reduce debt and improve the balance sheet.
A significant volume spike accompanied by a breakout above the recent support level, suggesting institutional interest.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a clear regulatory decision, a positive resource report, or a sharp increase in trading volume that exceeds 1.5 times the average. A price move above the last high of the crash zone would also confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score indicates a tight compression, so a breakout is likely to be sharp. Confirmation will come when the price clears the last support and volume backs it up.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is a deep crash bottom (likely >70% down). If the regulatory barrier is cleared and the mine proves viable, the stock could rebound to roughly the middle of its recent range, delivering about a 45% upside from the current price. The signal framework shows that deep crashes have historically produced the highest returns, and the large shareholder buying suggests smart‑money interest.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risks are the ongoing suspension, the lack of proven commercial production, and the company’s heavy debt load. If the mine never becomes viable or if the company faces delisting, the stock could stay at the bottom or decline further, wiping out the remaining capital.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk is limited to the current price level (the worst you can lose is the entire investment). Upside potential is roughly 45% if the price reaches the mid‑range. This gives a risk‑to‑reward ratio of about 1:4.5, which is attractive for a contrarian strategy.
